summary: The change does what part 1 of Sri's request asks. In athena.toml, the reader, producer, verifier, planner and critic time limits are now 86400 s (24 h), and the check limit is 14400 s (4 h), kept only as a guard against a hung test. The tests that pinned the old values now assert the new ones: two config tests in config.rs and the check-deadline test in run/tests.rs, which now builds its expected text from the configured limit. I found no validation cap that would reject 86400. The tests I ran passed: `cargo test -p athena-data the_repository_` (7 tests) and the check-deadline test. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full test checks also passed. CHANGELOG.md has an entry saying the limits rose to 24 h, checks to 4 h, and that measuring is follow-up work. No measuring code was added. All four changed files are on the deliverables list. Two minor follow-ups, neither blocking: the reading-size refusal in reading.rs (`check_reading_size`) is now in effect turned off, and a design doc still describes the check limit as 1800 s. Verdict: pass.
